briefing.opening: Good morning/afternoon, everyone. I will now begin the climate briefing for August 21, 2026.

sections.title: 🔴 Deepening Climate Crisis: Global Impacts and Warnings
sections.content: According to news collected today, the impacts of the climate crisis are intensifying globally. In Germany, this year's heatwave has caused 14,000 deaths, marking the largest scale on record [1], and across Europe, warnings have emerged that climate change is 'fueling' wildfires, potentially increasing the affected area by 39% [3, 125]. In a European village that recorded its highest temperature, residents reported that climate change is already reshaping daily life, highlighting its severity [117]. The likelihood of boreal forests transforming from evergreen to deciduous trees is increasing [119], and changes in natural ecosystems are accelerating, such as severe snow droughts in western regions being linked to climate change [123]. Domestically, a major flood caused by climate change occurred in Geoje, leading to the activation of emergency support camps [14], suggesting an urgent need to prepare for an era of extreme weather and heatwaves [22].

sections.title: 🌱 Domestic Efforts for Carbon Neutrality: Education, Support, and Technological Innovation
sections.content: Amidst the climate crisis, various domestic efforts continue towards achieving carbon neutrality. The Gyeonggi Provincial Office of Education is continuously expanding school complex facilities, including survival swimming pools and climate change experience centers, for students and local residents [2, 7], and Dongdaemun-gu operates climate crisis disaster education programs that link history with traditional Korean medicine [15]. Notably, the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism is collaborating with the popular webtoon 'Yumi's Cells' to operate a carbon neutrality experience center in Hongdae, encouraging the public to easily and enjoyably recognize and practice carbon neutrality [25, 28, 31, 35, 36, 39, 41, 47, 48, 49, 50, 52, 55, 57, 58, 59, 60, 61, 63, 65, 67]. KDN is fulfilling its social responsibility by providing summer relief supplies to vulnerable groups affected by the climate change crisis [5, 8, 9, 10, 13], and Seongju County is strengthening its on-site response capabilities to create a safe working environment amidst heatwave conditions [6]. In technological innovation, 'floating solar' technology is being applied to dams in the Philippines, entering the global climate market [17], and 'biofood' is emerging as a solution to the climate crisis and food security, emphasizing the importance of fostering technology companies [18, 21].

sections.title: 🇰🇷 Accelerating Renewable Energy Transition: Policy Reforms and Expansion Efforts
sections.content: A major overhaul of the domestic renewable energy supply system, the first in 15 years, is laying the groundwork for a significant renewable energy transition [75, 77, 79, 85]. The government has allowed priority grid connection for renewable energy facilities and reformed the RPS (Renewable Portfolio Standard) for the first time in 15 years, establishing a legal basis for transitioning to a contract market [83]. Concurrently, the Gyeonggi Provincial Council emphasized the need for institutional improvements and linkage with policy finance to expand renewable energy in Pyeongtaek City [74, 90, 102, 113], and four bills supporting resident-participatory renewable energy grid connection, proposed by Assemblyman Kim Joo-young, passed the National Assembly plenary session [88, 105]. SGI Seoul Guarantee is collaborating with the Korea Energy Agency and others to support rooftop solar guarantee insurance premiums [82, 106, 107, 110, 112, 116], and policies encouraging private and citizen participation are being implemented, such as households being able to sell solar power they produce starting in August [84]. Jeonju City is exploring an 'Energy Citizen Income' model where citizens produce solar power and share the profits [80, 94, 99, 103, 109, 114], and KORAIL plans to expand solar power generation in idle railway spaces to produce 116.9 GWh of renewable energy annually [100].

sections.title: ⚠️ Challenges and International Trends in Renewable Energy Transition
sections.content: As the transition to renewable energy accelerates, challenges that need to be addressed are also emerging. The projected electricity demand for 2040 increased by 26.8 million kW in just four months, leading to arguments that renewable energy alone will be insufficient [73], and amid discussions on renewable energy's variability, the view that an additional amount of power equivalent to 19 nuclear power plants is needed has also been raised [95]. In Asia, a one-year delay in power grid construction is expected to result in a $2.6 billion loss, making the securing of 'electricity pathways' a more critical issue than building power plants [104]. Meanwhile, regarding international efforts to address climate change, China is briefing on its oil and gas plans, President Xi Jinping's remarks on climate change, and its five-year coal plan, seeking its own strategy for energy transition [120, 121]. However, news that the University of Houston has cut 40% of its core curriculum, including climate change research, raises concerns by once again highlighting the importance of research and educational support needed for climate change response [124].

briefing.closing: Today's briefing has highlighted the severe impacts of the climate crisis, along with various domestic and international efforts to overcome it. This is a time when wise responses for a sustainable future are becoming even more crucial. This concludes today's climate briefing.
